title: Per-path usage journeys & chargeback — Console cost attribution demo
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-13 09:00 PDT | Recorded: yes | Duration: ~1:02
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Mehta (Redwood Solutions), Maya Singh (Pelagia Head ML), Derek Bloom (Pelagia Platform), Sara Ito (Pelagia FinOps), Tom Keller (Pelagia CTO)
---
Summary: Quick product demo focused on per-path / per-feature usage telemetry, route-level cost attribution for chargeback to product teams, and brief discussion of hosted vs dedicated implications for their regulatory workloads. Customer requested example of cost split by environment (prod vs staging) and per-model variant.
Topics: console overview, per-path dashboards, cost attribution matrix, tagging/labels, SSO + audit logs, pilot next steps
Action items (recorded inline below)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: okay everyone, thanks for joining, uh, Pelagia team, I think we have about an hour. I'm Lena, I'm the AE, and Jonah our systems engineer will walk through the console.
[00:18] Maya Singh: hi thanks, appreciate it. we got a small agenda in the invite. mainly curious how we can map usage to our product lines and do chargeback.
[00:34] Jonah Ruiz: great, i'll share my screen — give me 2 secs — so what you'll see first is the Usage Lenses page, this is an opinionated view we use to show traffic by path, by model, and by environment. you can filter by tag, route name, or customer id.
[00:52] Jonah Ruiz: (screen) ok, zooming into per-path, notice the left column shows recent sequence length distribution — that helps when thinking about cost per token.
[01:20] Derek Bloom: quick Q — can we map that to kubernetes namespaces or is it only via route tags?
[01:33] Jonah Ruiz: right now we rely on routetag and metadata that you send on request, but we also have an ingestion sidecar that can attach k8s namespace if you pass the header or via our agent. sometimes the transcript says "K-V cache" but it's actually KV cache — sorry fyi.
[01:55] Maya Singh: ha yeah we've seen kv cash in older docs.
[02:10] Jonah Ruiz: no worries. so here, per-path view shows total tokens, mean latency, and cost estimate — we calculate cost using your billing profile or our standard hosted pricing if you want a quick estimate.
[02:41] Sara Ito: do you support per-environment split? i.e. prod vs staging? we want to show FinOps the staging leakage cost.
[02:56] Jonah Ruiz: yes — you can tag requests with environment:prod/stage and we'll split. there's also a prebuilt dashboard for 'dev leakage' that highlights high-volume non-prod usage.
[03:20] Tom Keller: is the cost model customizable? our infra team uses custom GPU rates and preemptible pricing across clouds.
[03:35] Lena Park: good question. Jonah?
[03:39] Jonah Ruiz: yep, you can upload a cost profile — per-VM or per-GPU-hour — or connect our billing connector to your cloud billing to surface actual unit costs. we merge token-level telemetry with unit costs to give route-level spend. sometimes the automatic mapping mislabels model names, we call that model aliasing, you can set canonical ids.
[04:05] Maya Singh: curious about granularity — can we break down by model variant (quantized vs fp16) and by whether KV cache hit occurred?
[04:20] Jonah Ruiz: yes. we capture model variant as part of the request metadata and cache-hit as boolean. the Console shows a pivot table you can slice to see cost delta when cache hits vs misses. this is helpful to compute ROI of prefix caching.
[04:47] Derek Bloom: earlier you mentioned dedicated vs hosted — our security team is leaning private for PHI; any cost/latency tradeoffs we should expect?
[05:02] Jonah Ruiz: short answer: private gives you VPC control, KMS integration for keying, and audit logs; however, it can be more expensive per token depending on your GPU utilization. the Console has a simulator — you can run a hypothetical to compare unit economics between hosted catalog model variants and a dedicated cluster with custom quant profiles.
[05:36] Maya Singh: can we plug in our SSO? we use Okta and require SAML with SCIM provisioning and role mappings.
[05:50] Lena Park: yes — SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported; audit logs export to your SIEM. we also have SOC 2 Type II report available and an ISO doc if needed.
[06:06] Tom Keller: any data residency features? we already have EU customers and need to pin inference to a europe region.
[06:18] Jonah Ruiz: yes you can set routing policies by region and pin workloads to regions. we also support a private control plane for on-prem or VPC deployments if you need full data residency.
[06:35] [08:01] Jonah Ruiz: jumping back to the dashboard: here's an example report we prepared for a hypothetical healthcare customer — you'll see rows by route: intake-nlu, notes-summarizer, triage-assistant. each row has columns: total tokens, avg latency, cost estimate, and owners (tagged).
[08:25] Maya Singh: owners column is nice — we want to attribute to product teams. can owners be auto-populated from our internal team directory?
[08:37] Jonah Ruiz: yes if you map route tags to team ids via API or via our CSV mapping import.
[08:46] Sara Ito: on chargeback, can we generate monthly chargeback exports for our ERP? csv or parquet?
[08:58] Jonah Ruiz: both — CSV, Parquet, and we also have a billing API to push pre-batched chargeback lines. we can include labels for project, cost center, and environment.
[09:15] [09:46] Maya Singh: i noticed the console estimated cost per token — how confident should we be in these estimates vs actual cloud spend?
[09:58] Jonah Ruiz: depends on how accurate your cost profile is. if you map to real cloud billing, our estimates converge to your actual spend; the heuristic built-in is conservative but approximate. there's a reconciliation tool that highlights mismatches and the likely causes: rounding, batch sizing differences, or kernel-level perf variance.
[10:30] Derek Bloom: can we get lineage — like see which commit or service produced a spike in requests?
[10:42] Jonah Ruiz: yes if you pass a request-level commit hash or deployment id. we also ingest APM traces if you want deeper lineage.
[11:01] [11:45] Jonah Ruiz: switching to the 'Route Health' view — this is per-path SLOs, error rates, and cost burn. you can create alerts that trigger when cost per 1k tokens exceeds threshold or when latency SLOs degrade.
[12:12] Tom Keller: on SLOs — is there automatic throttling or fallback to a cheaper model when cost goes above a threshold?
[12:24] Jonah Ruiz: yes — routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants or route traffic to lower-cost region; there's also a 'graceful degrade' option that reduces max tokens for certain routes.
[12:48] [13:36] Maya Singh: this is helpful. on the security front, does Private deployment still show telemetry in your Console or do we host the console on our VPC?
[13:51] Lena Park: you can choose. for Private we offer a customer-hosted console option or a hybrid control plane where metrics flow to your telemetry endpoint only.
[14:07] Derek Bloom: what about KV cache visibility — can we see cache effectiveness per-route?
[14:20] Jonah Ruiz: yes — we show cache hit ratio and estimate token saved; sometimes transcription shows 'KV cash' as noted earlier...
[14:39] Sara Ito: (laughing) noted.
[15:05] [15:54] Maya Singh: let's talk pilot — we'd like to run a 6-week pilot across two product teams, validate chargeback and run reconciliation. how would you recommend scoping that?
[16:12] Lena Park: typical pilot: 1) onboarding + tagging for 2 routes, 2) 2–4 weeks of telemetry capture + baseline, 3) reconciliation and tuning of cost profiles, 4) a wrap-up dashboard and chargeback CSV. Jonah can help with the initial mapping and a small instrumenting script.
[16:40] Jonah Ruiz: i'd add we'll do a short performance bench for the main model variant to show latency delta with cache enabled. also propose an initial canary to confirm routing policies.
[17:05] Tom Keller: timeline wise — security needs to vet SOC2 and the network flow doc; they'll take 2 weeks. can we start tagging before that?
[17:18] Lena Park: yes, tagging work can start with dev accounts and doesn't require an approved security package.
[17:30] [18:10] Jonah Ruiz: demoing a saved report — here's 'Product Cost Matrix' which maps routes x teams with monthly cost and relative variance. you can export to chargeback format. it also shows an 'anomaly' column derived from our usage model. sometimes the analyzer misattributes to a legacy route name if the incoming route header uses an older alias.
[18:48] Maya Singh: is there an API for programmatically creating the dashboards? our internal dashboards are generated from infra-as-code.
[19:02] Jonah Ruiz: yes, Dashboard as Code via an API and Terraform provider is in beta — it supports creating lens, rules, alerts, and export jobs.
[19:24] Sara Ito: we have procurement questions: price for hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved cluster.
[19:36] Lena Park: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. quick summary: hosted is usage-based (per-token + downstream infra) with lower operational overhead; dedicated is reserved monthly capacity with a commitment discount.
[19:56] Derek Bloom: any competitors we should consider?
[20:06] Lena Park: a few common comparisons are Anthropic (managed API), doing self-hosted with toolkits like Triton, and other LLM platforms. note: we focus on production-grade inference economics and routing features.
[20:28] [21:02] Jonah Ruiz: jumping to the reconciliation tool example — you can upload your cloud billing CSV and we'll show a diff between expected token-based spend and billed spend by cluster. the UI marks the top 5 contributors to delta.
[21:40] Maya Singh: we already have a ticketing system for cost anomalies — can that hook into your alerts?
[21:52] Jonah Ruiz: yes — our alerts can push to PagerDuty, Slack, or your ticketing webhook (Jira).
[22:15] [22:47] Tom Keller: curious about how you estimate GPU utilization — is it sampled or exact?
[22:59] Jonah Ruiz: we take job-level utilization and sample GPU metrics; for dedicated clusters we can instrument more finely and use allocation info for precise cost calc.
[23:24] Maya Singh: any gotchas when instrumenting mobile clients — small inference calls from mobile can be noisy.
[23:35] Jonah Ruiz: tag mobile routes and run the dev leakage dashboard — you can also set per-route minima to avoid noise. there may be mis-indexed tokens if requests are truncated mid-stream in some SDK versions.
[23:58] [25:05] Lena Park: quick recap of what we'll deliver for pilot: onboarding guide, mapping spreadsheet, 6-week telemetry plan, weekly check-ins, and final chargeback CSV + reconciliation report.
[25:26] Maya Singh: good. can you also show a sample monthly export with cost center columns?
[25:40] Jonah Ruiz: we have an example — sending link in chat: https://redwood.con/exports/sample-chargeback-csv (placeholder).
[25:58] Derek Bloom: security requested to see network topology and KMS integration doc.
[26:10] Lena Park: we'll attach the security pack (SOC2, ISO, network flows, KMS diagrams). action item noted.
[26:28] [28:12] Jonah Ruiz: walking through alert config — here's an alert that triggers when per-route spend increases 30% month-over-month; you can auto-open a ticket to the owner. owner is another field you can set via tag.
[28:35] Sara Ito: how are owners resolved when a route has multiple owners?
[28:45] Jonah Ruiz: the UI supports multiple owners and a priority order; chargeback export can either split or attribute to a primary owner depending on your setting.
[29:02] Maya Singh: any recommended initial thresholds for us?
[29:12] Jonah Ruiz: for first 2 weeks keep thresholds broad (50% cost spike), then tighten after baseline.
[29:40] [31:00] Tom Keller: I'm thinking about the compliance timeline — if we go private, how long to provision?
[31:12] Lena Park: typical private provisioning is 4–6 weeks after contract; dedicated reserved cluster is 2–3 weeks depending on capacity. hosted account onboarding is immediate.
[31:35] Maya Singh: okay. are there any privacy-preserving features for training/embedding logs?
[31:47] Jonah Ruiz: we mask payloads, can redact PII at ingestion, and optionally don't store full prompts in the telemetry — we store hashes and metrics.
[32:05] [33:20] Jonah Ruiz: demoing the model-variant view — you can compare cost & latency for variants and the console will surface quantization recommendations. it can also show quality regressions if you run evals against a prompt set.
[33:49] Sara Ito: for chargeback we need a stable model id mapping across rollouts.
[33:59] Jonah Ruiz: yep, pin model versions in the deployment config; Console tracks lineage so you can see when a route switched model.
[34:22] [35:06] Maya Singh: anything else from your side?
[35:12] Tom Keller: one more procurement: sample contract with SLAs?
[35:20] Lena Park: we'll include SLA options in the pricing packet.
[35:36] [36:10] Jonah Ruiz: last bit — quick look at the API: you can push a metadata header 'x-rdwd-route' and 'x-rdwd-owner' and that will show up in the dashboard. sample curl in chat.
[36:30] Maya Singh: thanks, that's helpful.
[36:48] [37:50] Jonah Ruiz: ok sending the pilot outline and the mapping template in the follow up.
[38:12] (short silence / some cross talk)
[39:05] Maya Singh: sounds good. can we get a short bench on our typical prompt set — 1k concurrent users, avg seq len 300?
[39:20] Jonah Ruiz: yes, we'll run a focused bench using your sample prompt set and return latency results and cost delta with caching.
[39:40] Sara Ito: do you have any references from other healthcare customers?
[39:52] Lena Park: we can share anonymized case study and a contact if you'd like an intro.
[40:06] Derek Bloom: ok.
[40:20] [41:00] Lena Park: cool — we've captured next steps. anyone else have questions?
[41:12] Tom Keller: not for now.
[41:23] Maya Singh: no. thanks everyone.
[41:30] [42:00] Jonah Ruiz: wrap up: we'll deliver pilot pack, run bench, and send security docs.
[42:12] Lena Park: i'll send calendar invites for weekly check-ins and the pricing sheet.
[42:25] (meeting ends)
---
